classification.difficultyReason: Students tally the supplied observations and transfer their frequencies to an already labelled, evenly spaced scaffold. This directly applies the taught construction procedure; the number of observations adds counting care without requiring a new connection.

inlines.text: Display this data as a dot plot.

spec.description: Blank consecutive 20–29 number line with vertical alignment guides and room for seven dots.

answer.worked: Count each value, including the first 25. Label every integer from 20 to 29 at equal intervals. Stack one equal-sized dot for each observation. The frequencies, in order, are $2,2,4,3,2,7,5,5,3,1$, giving 34 dots.

spec.description: Complete dot plot with consecutive black ticks 20–29 and dashed grey alignment guides. Standard blue identifies observations only.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; question supplies the matching blank scaffold.
